scenes.setting: A hotel room over Pritz Harbor: Klein writes to Mr. Azik (the Card of Blasphemy, the copper whistle from the coffin elder, the Machinery Hivemind), hands the letter to a four-metre bone messenger, and pockets the papers of his new identity — a bounty hunter named Gehrman Sparrow. 'A hunter of evil…'
scenes.text_anchor: his name was Gehrman Sparrow.

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog before the gathering: Creeping Hunger releases the soul of the Faceless it ate — a middle-aged man with a blurry face — who answers about live mermaids, names the Secret Order, screams that Zaratul is 'an undying monster', and points at the Cathedral of Serenity before dissolving; the Faceless characteristic is left on the bronze table to sell through The World
scenes.text_anchor: “The Secret Order. I belong to the Secret Order.”

scenes.setting: The Tarot Gathering opens from Fors's seat: three figures across the mottled table, the great smog and the plague still on her mind, Prince Edessak dead as foretold — then Justice's greeting, 'You saved Backlund again!', and a baffled Moon
scenes.text_anchor: “You saved Backlund again!”

scenes.setting: The gathering continues mid-session: Emlyn and Alger puzzle over how Mr. Fool 'saved Backlund'; Audrey bows to thank Mr. World for the advance warning and credits Mr. Fool's adorer with stopping the Demoness of Despair and the True Creator's descent, then explains the follow-up diary pages are delayed; Fors conjures three pages of Roselle's diary and passes them up the bronze table; Klein belatedly introduces 'a new member, Mr. Moon'
scenes.text_anchor: Mr. World, if it wasn’t for your advance warning

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude: 11th February -- the Sauron family's Hunter pathway turns women into men at Sequence 4, Roselle wants to ridicule Floren; the modified artillery banquet; then 5th May, 'that unspeakable organization' gathers again and the old gentleman beside Roselle names himself Hermes -- the creator of ancient Hermes (reading continues into ch485)
scenes.text_anchor: 11th February. Today, I found out about a secret of the Sauron family.

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude continues: Klein reels at a living Hermes among the Twilight Hermit Order; the second page -- Roselle's Spectator-pathway suspicions (Discerner, Author, Visionary), the organization's dreamscape gatherings, Hermes's unrecorded answer about 'authority'; Audrey meanwhile notices the Dark Emperor card is missing from the table; the last page -- Roselle's first noble ball and the daughter of Viscount Derilose
scenes.text_anchor: Hermes? That’s an ancient powerhouse…

scenes.setting: The pages vanish and Mr. Fool says 'You may begin': Audrey asks The Sun whether he has escaped the cycle; Derrick bows his thanks -- the 'Rose Redemption' key point on the mural and the Angel of Fate let the Chief break the repeated cycle of fate
scenes.text_anchor: “You may begin.”

scenes.setting: Derrick reports the sixth exploration in full: the little boy Jack came from Enmat Harbor, the Rose Redemption murals, the Chief's suspicion that Amon is the Angel of Time and the mural's Angel of Fate is Tail Devourer Ouroboros; Audrey asks Mr. Fool about the eight Kings of Angels and gets 'You will come into contact with it in the future'; then trades -- Fors sells Alger the Dragon-Eyed Sea Condor lead for 2,000 pounds and Emlyn asks how a Sanguine can grow stronger, drawing every stare
scenes.text_anchor: “Mr. Sun, what are the titles of the other six Kings of Angels and their names?”

scenes.setting: Emlyn declares 'I am a pure Sanguine' and bickers with Derrick over whose history is older; Alger offers him a Sanguine baron's characteristic (4,000-5,000 pounds); Audrey buys the Tree of Elders fruit and Mirror Dragon blood from Emlyn via a sacrifice to Mr. Fool; The World offers Justice a Psychiatrist characteristic and asks The Hanged Man to sell the Faceless characteristic on commission, and Audrey preorders the resulting item
scenes.text_anchor: “Yes, I am a pure Sanguine.”

scenes.setting: Alger accepts Justice's preorder and marvels at her wealth; he asks for a way to put a whole ship's crew to sleep (Emlyn will ask the Sanguine); The World lists his needs -- ancient wraith spirituality and six-winged gargoyle eyes -- and Derrick promises the monster list once home; free discussion opens with Audrey asking Mr. Fool the truth behind the Great Smog and Prince Edessak
scenes.text_anchor: which one of you has a way or item to make everyone on board a ship sleep at the same time?

scenes.setting: The World tells The Hanged Man he has found Baelen -- reddish-brown skin, Southern Continent descent, Backlund accent, a fake third tooth -- seen meeting a masked MI9 man loyal to the royal family; Alger pays 100 pounds and connects it to Prince Edessak
scenes.text_anchor: “Mr. Hanged Man, I discovered the Baelen person you mentioned.”

scenes.setting: The World asks The Sun whether the City of Silver knows ancient Hermes; behind an isolation barrier Audrey reports the Psychology Alchemists were founded on the ruins of Hermes, and Mr. Fool warns her that Hermes is a member of the Twilight Hermit Order; the barrier lifts as the gathering winds toward its close
scenes.text_anchor: “Kid, do you know ancient Hermes?”

scenes.setting: The Tarot Gathering winds down: The Sun asks what hand gesture should thank Mr. Fool, Justice proposes secret identification signals and The Hanged Man shoots the idea down (traitors could fish members out one by one); Derrick concludes 'He' never mentioned gestures to protect them. 'Let us end today's gathering here' -- everyone stands and bows, Emlyn a beat late
scenes.text_anchor: Let us end today’s gathering here.

scenes.setting: Back among the dolls in his room, Emlyn replays his first Tarot Gathering member by member -- The Sun only a Sequence 8, Justice very rich, Miss Magician quiet, the Hanged Man a mature gentleman, The World unlikeable but impressive -- then remembers the 4,000-5,000-pound relic and the barony hanging over him
scenes.text_anchor: completely calm down as he recalled his first Tarot Gathering

scenes.setting: Alone in the palace above the fog, Klein lays out Lanevus's badge ('January 4th, 1350, 8 p.m. in Babur Valley') and coin-divines whether attending the gathering is risky -- the coin stands on its edge (no information at all) -- so he decides not to go in person, but to get involved from a distance tomorrow at 8 p.m.
scenes.text_anchor: It’s risky to attend the gathering in Babur Valley.

scenes.setting: 4th January, 10:35 a.m., the Pritz Harbor hotel room: The Hanged Man's 100 pounds has arrived; Klein dons Creeping Hunger as a black glove, boxes the Biological Poison Bottle, hides the Sun Brooch in his cigarette case, loads purifying, demon-hunting and exorcism bullets, and walks out fully armed with cane and suitcase
scenes.text_anchor: he was fully armed.

scenes.setting: The Pritz Harbor Ticket Company in White Rose Borough: an old three-story building with a notice board at the door -- lines enforced, no spitting, find the guard if there's a dispute, and 'Do not open canned wolf-fish in any of the rooms!'
scenes.text_anchor: Canned wolf-fish? What’s that?

scenes.setting: The ticket company lobby, seven windows and long queues: a bronze-skinned ex-navy guard talks Klein's ear off -- fifteen years at sea, night school, four children, the canned wolf-fish that emptied the hall -- then sells him on the White Agate (steam plus sail, 16 knots, Captain Elland his old boss) and its first-class cabins. Klein asks what advice he has for a maritime adventurer
scenes.text_anchor: Do you know anything about the White Agate?

scenes.setting: 'Adventurer?' -- heads turn in the queue; Klein traces a gaze to a boorish man in his thirties in a black top hat with pale blue eyes (the ex-adventurer he will meet on deck as Cleves). The guard's three pieces of advice: do not provoke pirates, do not provoke pirates, do not provoke pirates -- and don't be fooled by island girls; treasure legends are all fake
scenes.text_anchor: First, do not provoke pirates. Second, do not provoke pirates. Third, do not provoke pirates!

scenes.setting: Second-class ticket for the White Agate bought; back at the hotel Klein tries Pritz Harbor's famous fried fish and waits for night
scenes.text_anchor: After buying a second-class ticket for the White Agate

scenes.setting: Just before eight above the gray fog, Lanevus's badge in hand as the medium: 'The situation of the gathering this time.' The dream divination shows the Tussock River valley and about a dozen light-shrouded figures -- one of them black-haired, green-eyed, familiar: Leonard Mitchell! (visions only: the Babur Valley gathering, Leonard Mitchell)
scenes.text_anchor: Leonard Mitchell!

chapters_detail.title: The Sherlock Moriarty in the Investigation Report

scenes.setting: Above the fog, the dream shatters: Klein flips a coin -- it really is Leonard Mitchell, his Tingen Nighthawks teammate, at the Babur Valley gathering. Investigator for the Church, or hunting his revenge target behind the Nighthawks' backs? No way to tell; he draws a crimson moon and wishes him luck
scenes.text_anchor: Is it really Leonard, or a Faceless disguised as Leonard?

scenes.setting: A secret room under Backlund's Steam Cathedral: Archbishop Horamick Haydn hears the Machinery Hivemind deacons and captains report. Ikanser's file clears Sherlock Moriarty as an innocent 'hero of Backlund' (fraudulent expense claims aside); Trissy Cheek, Funkel and the underground ruins remain open. Ikanser is ordered to ask Arrodes and the mirror shows how Sherlock met Azik Eggers (visions only: Sherlock Moriarty, Old Kohler, the budget-hotel owner in the mirror); Arrodes's question is oddly gentle and Ikanser answers 'Yes'
scenes.text_anchor: In any case, Sherlock Moriarty is a hero of Backlund.

scenes.setting: 5th January, 9:00 a.m., Rose Wharf: the White Agate with its chimneys, sails and twelve cannons; armed sailors line the gangway under Captain Elland Kag's arrangement, and Klein climbs the hanging ladder with suitcase and cane. 'My travels begin...'
scenes.text_anchor: My travels begin…

scenes.setting: On the White Agate's deck a boorish man in a black half top hat and windbreaker comes straight to Klein -- 'Cleves, a former adventurer', now a bodyguard escorting his employer's family to the Rorsted Archipelago -- and points them out across the deck: a plump ruddy gentleman, a veiled lady, a boy under ten and a freckled girl of 15 or 16, three servants, two more bodyguards. 'Gehrman Sparrow.' Klein reads the greeting as a territorial warning between professionals
scenes.text_anchor: Cleves, a former adventurer.

scenes.setting: Klein's small second-class cabin with a window: he unpacks, the ship sails, and he thinks through how to act as a Faceless -- 'you can disguise yourself as anyone, but you are ultimately yourself'; a superficial disguise like Ince Zangwill's face digested nothing, so the real acting may be replacing a person on a social level
scenes.text_anchor: You can disguise yourself into anyone, but you are ultimately yourself.

scenes.setting: A quiet corner of the deck after the first hour: Cleves oils his trident, dagger and short knife ('There are children in the cabin'), warns that at sea guns alone aren't enough, and approves when Klein says he wouldn't fight boarding pirates -- 'The bounty hunters who travel the earth are often unable to be adventurers at sea.' Flying fish leap in the sun; Klein wonders how they taste
scenes.text_anchor: At sea, guns alone aren’t enough.

scenes.setting: The Steam Cathedral basement, second question to Arrodes: the mirror replays Sherlock Moriarty's charge at the altar, the brass key, Mr. A knocked flat and the two of them floating in the Tussock River before Mr. A vanishes (visions only: Sherlock Moriarty, Mr. A). Arrodes is back on form -- 'Who was the person you gave your all to...' -- Ikanser chooses punishment and takes a greenish lightning bolt; Horamick sighs 'A Grade 0 Sealed Artifact?' and nobody volunteers for the third question
scenes.text_anchor: I choose punishment.

scenes.setting: Night at sea, the cabin ceiling veiled in crimson moonlight: Klein wakes to his spiritual intuition, hears unnatural sounds outside, pulls on gloves and coat, coin-divines no danger, pockets the revolver from under his pillow and slips out toward the upper deck
scenes.text_anchor: Is someone having a rendezvous?

scenes.setting: The upper deck under the crimson moon, a faint smell of blood: Cleves is rigging a private hunt for a murloc that tried to climb aboard -- pig organs, pepper granules, mint-cream poison on his blades, two borrowed rifles -- while the female bodyguard Cecile and the employer's children Donna and Denton squat in the cabin's shadow. 'Uncle, are you also an adventurer?' Klein agrees to mind the children so Cecile isn't distracted
scenes.text_anchor: Cecile wasn’t careful enough and ended up waking Donna and Denton up.

scenes.setting: The White Agate's deck under the red moon: Klein squats with Donna and Denton while Cleves baits the rail with peppered pig organs and he and Cecile take up rifles; the murloc climbs aboard, eats, is shot, hurls Cleves off its trident, and is nearly over the side when a shot from elsewhere takes its eye and the mint poison finishes it
scenes.text_anchor: Cleves pulled the trigger, and a bullet flew out from the rifle.

scenes.setting: Captain Elland Kag steps out of the shadows with a smoking antique musket, buys the murloc for a fair 150 pounds ('Just Elland'), slices the cheek meat raw for the children and Klein, and proposes a night of grilled murloc, wine and sea legends
scenes.text_anchor: He was the captain of the White Agate, Elland Kag.

scenes.setting: Grilled murloc on deck: the cook bastes the belly meat while Elland pours Sonia blood wine, Klein and Cleves stick to black tea, the siblings get iced tea; Klein recalls his own Tingen murloc hunt (memory only: Old Neil, Swain), Elland toasts 'May the Storm be with us!', warns of Admiral Hell Ludwell and Admiral of Blood Senor, and starts the six treasure legends with the Death's Key and the Fountain of Unaging
scenes.text_anchor: “To a beautiful night. May the Storm be with us!”

scenes.setting: The same deck dinner, continued: Elland remembers meeting Nast's ship in the Strait of Calamity, describes Agalito's corpse-pale bounty notice, and runs through the Solomon inheritance, the Specter Empire, the Lost City of Newins and the Sunken Laurel; everyone says what they would do with millions ('Return home'), Klein says 'Hurry up and wake up', and Cleves adds Roselle's last secret trove
scenes.text_anchor: “Fountain of Unaging? Will you really gain eternal youth if you drink it?”

scenes.setting: Last course on deck: Desi grilled murloc belly, Klein's gourmet verdict and Donna's newspaper-column idea, a final toast, mermaid/Siren talk from Cleves, then Cecile sends the children to bed and Cleves tells Denton to train for five years before asking about adventuring
scenes.text_anchor: “Desi grilled fish, it’s different from how you usually eat it.”

scenes.setting: Walking back into the cabin: Cleves hands Gehrman Sparrow two five-pound notes for 'taking care of the children'; Klein accepts so as not to look like a greedy madman, and the group goes inside
scenes.text_anchor: “Your payment.”

scenes.setting: Klein alone at the rail under the red moon, the gloom of Backlund's smog lifting off him; he wants to sing and can't remember the verses. 'What a beautiful night.'
scenes.text_anchor: “What a beautiful night.”

scenes.setting: The exploratory team returns to the City of Silver after getting lost; Derrick stares at the weed-cracked wall in a trance while Demon Hunter Colin presses his temple with a lost look before recovering
scenes.text_anchor: the exploratory team returned to the City of Silver.

scenes.setting: Backlund, the White family home: Emlyn asks his parents who knows Sanguine history; his father (doctorate in medicine, gold-rimmed glasses) names the sleeping Lord Nibbs, then the self-styled historian Waymandy, whom Emlyn resolves to visit
scenes.text_anchor: “No one in Backlund knows more than Lord Nibbs.”

scenes.setting: Two days later the White Agate docks at Damir Harbor; Klein arms himself with every mystical item and heads ashore for a bar, crossing Donna, Denton, Cleves and the family on their way to a cured-meat restaurant
scenes.text_anchor: The whistle sounded and the White Agate sailed into Damir Harbor.

scenes.setting: Flying Fish & Wine, its front plastered with bounty notices from 800,000 pounds down; inside it is abnormally quiet -- Captain Elland at the bar and two large men squared off in the middle of the room
scenes.text_anchor: Flying Fish & Wine… Klein looked at the signboard

scenes.setting: The standoff: a bare-armed Navy sailor with a dagger versus shaved, sea-eagle-tattooed Sea Eagle Logan with a museum-piece musket; Elland explains the Black Tulip rumour, Klein orders a Southville beer, the bouncer separates the pair, the sailor leaves, and Elland heads upstairs to play cards ('don't trust anyone here' -- 'Including you?')
scenes.text_anchor: “One glass of Southville beer.”

scenes.setting: A short, wretched-looking man sits down and pitches a Specter Empire treasure scheme (15 companions, 720 pounds raised) with a stack of brown letters -- until Sea Eagle Logan strides over and hurls 'Woody, you damn sewer rat' across the floor
scenes.text_anchor: “Have you heard of the Specter Empire?”

scenes.setting: Logan's cured-meat shakedown (five pounds, 'you offered to treat me'); Gehrman Sparrow answers 'Why don't you just rob me?', breaks Logan's jaw and teeth with fist, knee and revolver butt, pays with Logan's own money, learns from the bartender that Logan invented his Admiral Hell connection, collects two months of sea rumours over the meat, slams the bartender's head into the bar as 'today's lesson', throws Logan at the bouncers and slips out
scenes.text_anchor: “Why don’t you just rob me?”

scenes.setting: Out in the streets of Damir Harbor, changing direction again and again, Klein slows and a gold coin starts weaving through his fingers as if scouting
scenes.text_anchor: a gold coin appeared in his hand.

scenes.setting: A dark alley off the Damir Harbor seafront, minutes after Klein fled Flying Fish & Wine: the gold coin picks his turn, he calls out the tail — a black-cloaked man of about thirty who pitches him a pirate crew's creed, annual leave and treasure hunts (Sunken Laurel, Roselle's Treasure), then introduces himself as Rear Admiral Iceberg's fourth boatswain, Blazing Danitz; Klein's killing intent through Creeping Hunger makes him tremble and answer where White Shark lives
scenes.text_anchor: “Rear Admiral Iceberg Edwina Edwards’s subordinate, fourth boatswain of the Golden Dream, Blazing Danitz.”

scenes.setting: Klein gone: Danitz straightens up in the alley, takes off his cloak — 'What a terrifying fellow' — and resolves to telegraph his Captain in the morning about a new terrifying person at sea; White Shark's fate is not his concern
scenes.text_anchor: “What a terrifying fellow…”

scenes.setting: Another quiet street: Klein examines the black glove — Creeping Hunger's sealed hunger stirred when he wanted to kill Danitz — divines that Danitz did not lie and that White Shark cannot harm him, then reshapes his face into a blond, blue-eyed stranger, untucks his shirt and heads back to the bar
scenes.text_anchor: He instantly changed his appearance—blond hair, blue eyes, and ordinary facial features!

scenes.setting: On the way back to Flying Fish & Wine the disguised Klein passes Blazing Danitz, who glances once without recognizing him and heads for the hotel opposite; Klein checks the bounty wall and pushes the bar door open less than ten minutes after escaping
scenes.text_anchor: On the way, he met Blazing Danitz again.

scenes.setting: Inside the bar: the bandaged bartender stands beside his boss — a tall, fat, bald, fair-skinned man like a white shark come ashore — who is pressing Captain Elland about 'his passenger'; Elland pats his sword, answers with a proverb about wild dogs and rats, and White Shark Hamilton settles for half the damages before slapping the bartender's teeth out while the blond stranger watches from five metres away
scenes.text_anchor: “… Just Elland, is this your answer?” White Shark Hamilton narrowed his eyes.

scenes.setting: Still in the bar: the bartender writhes on the floor, White Shark Hamilton stamps up the creaking stairs, the drunkards drift off, Captain Elland and his men go back upstairs to their cards — and the disguised Klein follows, meaning to squeeze the pirate-connected owner for information to feed Creeping Hunger's replacement souls
scenes.text_anchor: Klein took the opportunity to follow.

scenes.setting: The dark candle-lit second-floor corridor: Klein wipes his face into one of the downstairs bouncers, patches his clothes with Illusion Creation, walks past the card room and tells the corridor guards 'there's something going on downstairs again' before knocking on White Shark's door
scenes.text_anchor: “There’s something going on downstairs again.”

scenes.setting: White Shark Hamilton's room: 'Boss, it's me' gets Klein in; he drops the illusion back to the blond stranger and, radiating Creeping Hunger's starved-demon gaze, calls himself a hunter and offers two choices; Hamilton confesses he fences loot and gathers intelligence for the pirates via a 'radio transceiver' hidden behind a secret door, names Silver Coin Viper Oder and Admiral of Blood's intelligence officer Old Quinn as its source and Old Quinn as his potion-giver; Klein stages a fake exit, silently watches Hamilton tap out 'I was targeted!' — memorising the frequency and passcodes — and leaves for real
scenes.text_anchor: “One is to answer frankly. The second is to be killed by me and then answer honestly.”

scenes.setting: White Shark's room, moments after Klein leaves: Hamilton flings the door open on his bouncers swapping jokes, who insist only 'Lardero' went in and that the boss let him in himself — then slams it shut, leaving them suspecting he is drunk
scenes.text_anchor: “Yes, Lardero. He said that there was a situation downstairs.”

scenes.setting: Hamilton alone, pacing: from Qilangos-style shapeshifting he reasons his way to 'that guy is a novice, his madness is a disguise, his strength is a mystical item', re-sets the radio transceiver and telegraphs a profile of the blond, blue-eyed, 'a little timid' target — pleased that greedy sharks will finish the young man for him
scenes.text_anchor: That guy is a novice! His madness is a disguise!

scenes.setting: Night streets back toward the White Agate: sure nobody is following, Klein turns his face back into Gehrman Sparrow, tucks in his shirt, puts on the gold-rimmed glasses and chuckles — the whole clumsy-novice act was bait, and with the passcodes he can now monitor Old Quinn's traffic; he only needs Miss Justice or Miss Magician to buy him a receiver through The World
scenes.text_anchor: he turned his face back to Gehrman Sparrow as he passed through the shadows

scenes.setting: Outside the White Agate: Klein meets Donna's family and Cleves returning; Cleves has already heard of the trouble at Flying Fish & Wine, Donna's father introduces himself as Urdi Branch and shakes hands, Klein's Spirit Vision finds the family's gift boxes of Damir cured meat tinged with the spirit world, little Denton and Donna insist the moon is 'so very red' — then up the gangway to the deck, farewells, and a huge skeleton messenger drops a letter
scenes.text_anchor: “A colleague, Gehrman Sparrow,” Cleves introduced in a very simple manner.

scenes.setting: The White Agate's deck at night: the messenger collapses into a fountain of bones while Donna and Denton — their cured-meat Spirit Vision briefly open — stand agape; Klein hushes them with a finger, Cleves and Cecile sense something but see nothing, a coin toss says no harm done, and Klein lets himself into his second-class room
scenes.text_anchor: she saw that her brother was still in a daze. She quickly grabbed his arm and pushed his hand against his mouth.

scenes.setting: Alone in the cabin by a half-burnt candle: Klein opens Mr. Azik's reply — the Dark Emperor card and the copper whistle come back, and the letter recalls a mountain-tall Blood Emperor in a red cape and a revived Dark Emperor on a throne (memories only), warns him never to blow the whistle, mentions Feathermen, and teaches a sealing technique; Klein burns the letter, practises the seal, and rituals both items above the gray fog
scenes.text_anchor: “… That card that depicts the Dark Emperor reminds me of certain scenes.

scenes.setting: Early morning: after toast and lemon tea in the second-class cafeteria Klein takes the deck air and meets a drunk Captain Elland coming back; Elland waves off White Shark — he tipped him the few soli from last night's winnings — and Klein returns to the bow with a 'Thank you', finding it too hard to force a persona
scenes.text_anchor: “White Shark didn’t cause you any trouble, right?

scenes.setting: At the bow: puffy-eyed Donna and Denton, with Cecile a few paces off, ask 'who was that last-last night?'; Klein sells the four-metre messenger as a gentle postman, tells them they saw it because their hearts are pure, and the two solemnly promise to keep his secret
scenes.text_anchor: “Uncle, who was that last-last night?”

scenes.setting: A new Damir Harbor passenger walks onto the deck with a suitcase — Blazing Danitz in a wig with blackened eyebrows, holiday cut short to await orders at the Rorsted Archipelago — and freezes at the sight of the gentle, mad young adventurer beaming at him from the bow
scenes.text_anchor: Suddenly, he saw a familiar figure.

scenes.setting: The White Agate's deck: 'I've got a friend' — Klein leaves the children and walks up to the disguised Danitz, who chooses not to bolt; a cold interrogation (Rorsted Archipelago, first-class Room 312, 'Is there a servant room?') ends with one word, 'Hostage', and Danitz agreeing to sleep in the servant's room of his own cabin
scenes.text_anchor: Klein glanced at him and said one word in a faint voice, “Hostage.”

scenes.setting: Room 312 and back: Klein claims the master bedroom, marches Danitz down to the second-class cabin to pack Klein's things into the suitcase like a servant, and back upstairs gives him a name — 'Gehrman Sparrow' — before sitting on a hard chair and having the pirate list every famous pirate he knows, by bounty
scenes.text_anchor: “Gehrman Sparrow,” Klein responded succinctly.

scenes.setting: Noon on the open sea at 13 knots: a dry-mouthed Danitz leads Klein into the first-class restaurant, where Donna's family and Cleves are waiting at a large table — 'Uncle Sparrow!' from Denton, a puzzled Donna, a suspicious Cleves; 'He's treating,' says Klein, and Danitz grits out that Gehrman once saved him
scenes.text_anchor: “Uncle Sparrow!” Because of their shared secret, the little boy, Denton, had changed the way he addressed him.

scenes.setting: A window table: Danitz sighs over the fresh-food menu and a lobster anecdote, Klein draws a line by price — 'All of these' — greets Captain Elland as he passes through the dining room, and learns that Danitz once fought Elland's crew when he was boatswain of the Wilhelm V and still wonders why Just Elland, already an Arbiter, quit the Navy
scenes.text_anchor: “I’ve always wondered why Just Elland would suddenly quit the Navy. By then, he was already an Arbiter.”

scenes.setting: First-class dining room of the White Agate, noon: Klein eats through the whole menu at Danitz's expense while the pirate gossips about why Just Elland quit the Navy; a crewman stomps in with 'Captain, there's a pirate ship!' and Elland calmly sends the first-class passengers (Donna's family, Cleves) back to their cabins
scenes.text_anchor: “Captain, there’s a pirate ship!”

scenes.setting: Room 312: the Red Skull ship (Sea Wolf Johnson, One-Eyed Anderson) closes in; Klein makes Danitz remove his wig and makeup, then hang out of the window by his forearm so the pirates can see Rear Admiral Iceberg's fourth boatswain -- 'I'm a very easy person to get along with, really, as long as you do as I tell you.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Take off your wig,” Klein calmly ordered.

scenes.setting: On the Red Skull: a lookout reports 'a weird guy hanging out the window'; Sea Wolf Johnson raises his binoculars, recognizes Blazing Danitz, concludes the White Agate is Rear Admiral Iceberg's prey and orders everyone to stay far away
scenes.text_anchor: Isn’t that Blazing Danitz?

scenes.setting: Room 305: Cleves at the window with his revolver, Donna's family huddled in the living room with the bodyguards Cecile and Teague on guard -- then, after a few minutes, 'The pirates have left,' to Urdi Branch's confusion
scenes.text_anchor: “The pirates have left.”

scenes.setting: Room 312: Danitz crawls back in, snorting that Klein borrowed his captain's reputation and she hates that; Klein only asks whether her Loen bounty was 26,000 pounds
scenes.text_anchor: “You’re borrowing my captain’s reputation!

scenes.setting: The captain's quarters: a sailor reports the Red Skull has fled; Elland watches it vanish over the horizon, cannot explain it, and orders the navigator to dock at Bansy Harbor tonight and report the encounter to the Navy and the Church
scenes.text_anchor: “We shall dock at Bansy Harbor tonight.

scenes.setting: Room 305 after the all-clear: Teague and Cecile explain bounties to Donna and Denton (One-Eyed 500 pounds, Sea Wolf 900, 'nearly 1,000 pounds!'); the siblings privately decide Uncle Sparrow's house-tall messenger scared the pirates off and slip out into the corridor to go find him in Room 312
scenes.text_anchor: “Are the Red Skull pirates that powerful?”

scenes.setting: Room 312: Danitz, no longer mentioning Rear Admiral Iceberg, holds forth on why pirates will always survive the Navy's ironclads -- and Klein points at his suitcase: 'Wash the dirty clothes inside.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Wash the dirty clothes inside.”

scenes.setting: Donna and Denton visit Room 312 and find the famous pirate doing laundry; Klein tells them plainly he is 'my prisoner of war', a pirate -- Danitz blurts 'I'm Sieg!' and Klein overrides with 'Danitz.' The siblings leave, feeling the pirate's eyes are fierce
scenes.text_anchor: “To be exact, he’s my prisoner of war.”

scenes.setting: Back in Room 305 the siblings innocently ask about 'Danitz'; Cleves identifies Blazing Danitz, Rear Admiral Iceberg's fourth boatswain of the Golden Dream, bounty 3,000 pounds -- more than three times the Red Skull captain -- and goes quiet in recall
scenes.text_anchor: “3,000 pounds.”

scenes.setting: 6 p.m., Room 312: the White Agate enters Bansy Harbor; Danitz eyes the darkened harbor and the tall lighthouse -- 'Elland is very cautious. It seems like there are some nasty legends here.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Bansy Harbor? Elland is very cautious…”

scenes.setting: Room 312: Danitz recounts Bansy Harbor's legends -- 500 soldiers vanished in a fog 300 years ago, native cannibal rites to a self-made God of Weather, the custom of not opening doors on foggy nights, and blood cakes learned from elves; he suggests the Green Lemon Restaurant. Klein's coin divination says no dormant danger, but he still feels uneasy, shuts himself in the washroom and tells Danitz 'You can use this opportunity to escape' -- Danitz stays put
scenes.text_anchor: “Legend has it that 300 years ago when the Loen army first occupied this island

scenes.setting: Washroom, then above the gray fog: the spirit pendulum on 'There is danger dormant in Bansy Harbor' spins clockwise hard and fast -- great danger for Klein lurks in the port, though a second divination rules out any pirate-related mishap
scenes.text_anchor: “There is danger dormant in Bansy Harbor.”

scenes.setting: Back in the real world Klein resolves to stay hidden and safe: 'To the first-class dining room' -- Danitz, puzzled at the change of mind, doesn't argue
scenes.text_anchor: “To the first-class dining room”

scenes.setting: The gangway: Cleves sends Donna's family ahead to the Green Lemon Restaurant, saying he has a matter with Captain Elland first
scenes.text_anchor: “Head to the Green Lemon Restaurant first.

scenes.setting: Halfway back aboard Cleves meets Elland (straight sword at his waist) and announces 'I'm going to visit Gehrman Sparrow' -- Elland grasps the insurance behind the words and tells his first mate to wait fifteen minutes
scenes.text_anchor: “I’m going to visit Gehrman Sparrow.”

scenes.setting: Room 312 doorway: Cleves confronts the re-disguised Danitz -- 'Blazing Danitz?' -- who denies being the pirate worth 3,000 pounds; Klein says only that he is 'Watching over him', declines help, then gives Cleves a solemn warning: return to the ship soon, 'There is danger dormant in Bansy Harbor.'
scenes.text_anchor: “There is danger dormant in Bansy Harbor.”

scenes.setting: Second floor of the Green Lemon Restaurant: Donna sees Uncle Cleves arrive downstairs as gales rise over the 'Weather Museum'; through the window a man in a black cloak with a lantern turns to look up at her -- inside the cloak there is no head, only a bare neck spurting bright red blood
scenes.text_anchor: the area where the person’s head was supposed to be was empty inside the black cloak

scenes.setting: Green Lemon Restaurant, second floor: Donna stammers 'A headless zombie!'; Cecile rushes to the window and sees nothing, Urdi Branch bans her from 'Fonce's Horror Stories Anthology'
scenes.text_anchor: “A headless zombie!”

scenes.setting: Cleves comes up, takes Donna seriously ('It's okay, this shall pass'), and explains the Bansy custom of not going out or answering knocks on stormy nights; Donna notices the pale diners spooning dark red blood blocks with red-stained lips and prays to the Goddess for the gale to stop
scenes.text_anchor: “It’s okay, this shall pass.

scenes.setting: Bansy Harbor Telegraph Office: Elland and First Mate Harris finish their report to the Navy as the wind howls; the slow-spoken curly-haired clerk warns them 'you'll lose your head' if they go out, and Elland decides on the cathedral next door
scenes.text_anchor: Bansy Harbor Telegraph Office.

scenes.setting: Against the gale to the Storm cathedral: in the prayer hall a priest in dark blue sits before the Storm Sacred Emblem; Elland pats his shoulder -- 'Jayce, where's your bishop?' -- and the head wobbles, falls and rolls, blood fountaining from the neck to soak Elland's face (Jayce is a headless corpse, not tagged)
scenes.text_anchor: “Jayce, where’s your bishop?”

scenes.setting: 7:15 p.m., leaving the first-class restaurant as the wind eases: Klein asks the crew who is still ashore -- the Branch and Timothy families at the Green Lemon, and the Captain and First Mate at the telegraph office
scenes.text_anchor: “Who else isn’t back?”

scenes.setting: Room 312: Klein watches the wind-stirred waves, his spiritual intuition warning that something bad is brewing; five more minutes, still no Elland or Branch family; a glance makes Danitz sit up straight before Klein goes into the washroom
scenes.text_anchor: he still didn’t see Captain Elland and Donna’s family return.

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog: the pendulum on 'Bansy Harbor is dangerous' spins clockwise but slowly -- danger within acceptable limits, contradicting the earlier reading; Klein reasons the dormant danger is centuries old and only surfaces if something is triggered
scenes.text_anchor: “Bansy Harbor is dangerous.”

scenes.setting: Room 312: after a long hesitation Klein buttons his frock coat, takes hat and cane and tells Danitz 'You're free' -- he is going out for the captain and the ordinary people because 'They kept my secret for me. He treated me to murloc meat.' Danitz, realizing the anchored ship is no safer, runs after him; lantern in hand, they walk into the dim port
scenes.text_anchor: “You’re free.”

scenes.setting: Bansy Harbor's pitch-black streets in thin fog: a floating rotted head with sharpened teeth lunges at Klein's ear -- he bats it away with his cane and a pure ray of light from the sky vaporizes it; a second head shrugs off Danitz's bullet and fireball until he pops a small fireball inside its mouth, then he runs to catch up with the monster who didn't wait for him
scenes.text_anchor: It was a head that had lost its body

scenes.setting: Green Lemon Restaurant, second floor emptying out: Donna can't stomach the blood cakes; when the wind stops at 7:40 Cleves urges heading back at once and Urdi Branch pays and leads the family and bodyguards downstairs -- a creak from a side room makes Donna grab Denton's hand
scenes.text_anchor: “The wind has stopped!”

scenes.setting: Ground floor: the round-faced owner Mr. Fox advises 'It's fogged up. It's best not to go out'; the gentlemen and ladies who 'chose to stay' watch from their doorways as knocking and distant screams begin; remembering Gehrman Sparrow's warning, Cleves insists on the ship's cannons and opens the door once the knocking stops
scenes.text_anchor: “What are you trying to convey, Mr. Fox?”

scenes.setting: Outside, the restaurant door slams shut behind them; a shriveled rotting head crashes to the ground before Cleves -- then light falls from the sky and melts it into nothing while Urdi and the others tremble
scenes.text_anchor: It was a shriveled, rotting head!

scenes.setting: A lantern approaches through the fog: 'Uncle Sparrow!' -- Klein tosses the lantern to Danitz and, as if nothing were out of the ordinary, tells Cleves 'Let's go to the telegraph office first. What about the Timothys?'
scenes.text_anchor: “Uncle Sparrow!” Donna and Denton cried out.

scenes.setting: Bansy Harbor at night, outside the Green Lemon Restaurant: Klein (as Gehrman Sparrow) knocks three times, gets silence, and kicks the door in; the pudgy owner Fox stands with a revolver while the lodgers watch from their doorways; the Timothy couple are brought down from upstairs and choose to join the Branch family outside
scenes.text_anchor: “Where’s the Timothy family?”

scenes.setting: The walk to the telegraph office with a party of 15: Klein does a headcount, fires Sun Halo to steady everyone, tosses Azik's copper whistle as bait so three flying heads burn in Fire of Light, then nails a headless cloaked monster to the street with his cane and dissolves it with 'Sun!'; at the office door a woman's voice says the captain went to the cathedral and asks them to look out for her colleague Paavo Court
scenes.text_anchor: “His name… is Paavo Court.”

scenes.setting: Still at the telegraph office door: Klein asks what Paavo Court looks like and gets the chilling 'two eyes, two ears, a nose, and a mouth'; he refuses to probe further, states 'Storm cathedral', and leads the party through the thinning fog after another Sun Halo
scenes.text_anchor: “He has two eyes, two ears, a nose, and a mouth.”

scenes.setting: The Storm cathedral: Elland (sword and musket, boat-shaped hat) admits them after the White Shark password, first mate Harris unbars the door; the priest Jayce lies decapitated in the prayer hall, Bishop Millet and every servant are missing; Klein examines the corpse (no remnant spirit, a blue sapphire characteristic he leaves untouched) and decides to return to the ship
scenes.text_anchor: “The priest I knew, Jayce, died in there.

scenes.setting: Walking back past the telegraph office: a wheezing middle-aged man in a dark blue bishop robe staggers out of the fog -- Bishop Millet, claiming heathens revived the old sacrifice and that he was wounded in the fight; lightning flares on the mountain, but Klein's coin says 'He has ill intentions' and Millet's eyes flash dark red
scenes.text_anchor: “Bishop Millet?”

scenes.setting: The battle with the fallen bishop on the fog-bound street: Millet's hurricane scatters the party and six headless men charge; Klein throws the copper whistle as bait and the Sun Brooch to Elland ('Inject your spirituality. Five seconds. Holy water.'), dodges wind blades with Paper Figurine Substitutes, breaks Millet with Psychiatrist's Frenzy and Interrogator, burns him as a Priest of Light and lets Creeping Hunger devour what is left; Danitz's Fire Ravens smash Elland's flask of holy water over the headless men
scenes.text_anchor: “Inject your spirituality. Five seconds. Holy water.”

scenes.setting: Aftermath: Klein pockets Millet's thumb-sized characteristic, reloads, burns a paper figurine to scrub the traces and walks the shaken party back past the cracked ground to the telegraph office; a MAN now answers -- Paavo Court, 'Melanie's colleague', with Melanie's voice agreeing she is 'doing very well' -- the telegram draft comes under the door smelling of blood, and Klein orders 'Return to the ship.'
scenes.text_anchor: “I’m… Paavo Court, Melanie’s colleague.

scenes.setting: Back aboard the White Agate: Elland rallies his officers and readies the cannons, Donna and Denton are sent to their room ('Shh!'), and once the families are in the cabin Klein hands Elland the bishop's characteristic for the Mandated Punishers; Elland offers to tell the Church that Gehrman is with him and gets a 'Guess.' out of Danitz
scenes.text_anchor: “If there are still Mandated Punishers alive, return this to them.”

scenes.setting: The night watch on deck: the mountain flares with lightning and the fog lifts; three Mandated Punishers come to the dock, are divined genuine, take back Millet's characteristic and brief Elland -- Jayce found the cannibal cult, Millet was its fallen leader -- while Klein thinks of the voices behind the telegraph office door; dawn brings Bansy Harbor back to life
scenes.text_anchor: “The matter has been resolved. There aren’t any problems.”

scenes.setting: Morning, heading into the cabin as the White Agate's whistle sounds: Elland's idle remark that old 'Binsy' overlapped with modern Bansy Harbor freezes Klein -- Binsy Town is where the Backlund evil spirit said to look for the descendants of Medici, the King of Angels of Rose Redemption
scenes.text_anchor: “Binsy?”

scenes.setting: Klein sweats over how close he danced to Rose Redemption and a hidden Red Angel and resolves to report Bansy Harbor through The World at the coming gathering; Elland tosses him a small black box -- a murloc's bladder, 'Aren't we friends now?' -- then goes to sleep, and Klein leads Danitz to Room 312
scenes.text_anchor: “The bladder of the murloc.

scenes.setting: Room 312: Donna and Denton wait at the door, hand over 150 pounds from their parents and the Timothys, and ask what Beyonders are and whether they can become 'Superman' like Emperor Roselle described -- Klein rolls up his sleeves to show a shriveled arm, a translucent one and a face of pale flesh granules: 'This is madness.'
scenes.text_anchor: “This is madness.”

scenes.setting: The corridor outside Room 312: the children stumble out and fall; the door clangs shut behind them; Donna suddenly cannot stop crying -- 'I j-just feel very, very sad all of a sudden.'
scenes.text_anchor: “I j-just feel very, very sad all of a sudden.”

scenes.setting: Inside Room 312: Danitz says there was no need to scare the children like that -- and catches the blood-and-dirt-caked cane thrown at him: 'Wash it clean.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Wash it clean.”

scenes.setting: Backlund, the Hall mansion: the household packs to leave for East Chester County a week after the New Year Ball; Lady Caitlyn asks Audrey her plans (the Church's charity organizations), and Audrey teases Susie about the green pastures before checking the clock -- almost time for the Tarot Gathering
scenes.text_anchor: “Mother, I want to like to join the Church’s charity organizations.”

scenes.setting: Tarot Gathering opens above the gray fog: Emlyn arrives to Audrey greeting everyone in tarot order from The Fool to The World; Justice and The Magician each offer three new Roselle diary pages, The Sun hands over copied legends of ancient gods plus a monster list for The Hanged Man
scenes.text_anchor: “Honorable Mr. Fool, I’ve gotten another three Roselle diary pages~”

scenes.setting: Diary-reading interlude: Klein skims the six pages -- two are repeats, the other four are Roselle's money-obsessed period ('What did I invent today', 'How many gold coins can it be sold for')
scenes.text_anchor: Roselle’s diary and the legend of the ancient gods soon appeared in the palm of Klein’s hand.

scenes.setting: Gathering continues: Audrey spots the Dark Emperor card back at Mr. Fool's hand; Klein reads the City of Silver's legends of the eight ancient gods (Lilith as a mountain of flesh, ruler of the crimson moon), then 'You may begin' -- Emlyn sells Justice the fruit of the Tree of Elders and Mirror Dragon blood for 750 pounds, balks at the 4,500-pound Sanguine inheritance, and The Hanged Man sells Justice the Artisan's silver mask for 5,500 pounds, 4,500 of it to The World
scenes.text_anchor: “It costs 5,500 pounds.”

scenes.setting: Transactions wind up: Derrick's Spirit Eater stomach pouch for Fors, the Solar High Priest formula conjured for The Sun, Alger picks three City of Silver ingredients and asks Fors to ready the Dragon-Eyed Sea Condor eyeballs; free exchange -- Fors warns Backlund is still under pressure, The Hanged Man tells The Sun to check on the Chief before any ritual, and The World asks the ladies for a radio transceiver before mentioning the revived custom at Bansy Harbor and its corrupted Storms bishop
scenes.text_anchor: “Miss Magician, your Spirit Eater’s stomach pouch is ready.”

scenes.setting: Deep laughter from the end of the table: Mr. Fool says Bansy 'reminds me of a King of Angels' -- Medici, who established the Rose Redemption, whose descendants live in Binsy, the old name of Bansy; Fors despairs at the scale of it, Emlyn feels like a messiah, and Alger realizes Mr. Fool foresaw last week's promise about meeting the Kings of Angels
scenes.text_anchor: “Medici, who established the Rose Redemption. ‘His’ descendants live in Binsy.”

scenes.setting: Alger's chain of guesses: Mr. Fool is warning the Church of Storms through him, The World must be Mr. Fool's adorer-representative, and the Tarot Club is built to interfere in events; Audrey senses The World's strangeness and asks Medici's pathway -- 'Red Priest' -- while Klein congratulates himself on having set The World up as Sherlock Moriarty
scenes.text_anchor: “Red Priest.”

scenes.setting: Emlyn, broke, asks 'suppose a powerhouse arranged for you to investigate something...' and The Hanged Man tells him to display abnormalities and let himself be watched; Emlyn then sells Alger a can of anesthetic gas for the ghost-ship sailors; Mr. Fool foresees 'a new appearance of themselves next week' and closes the gathering
scenes.text_anchor: “Let us end today’s gathering here.”

scenes.setting: Backlund, Cherwood Borough: Fors back at her desk after the gathering, two days from her Spirit Eater pouch and Trickmaster; Xio slams the door on her way out again (heard, not seen); Fors decides to write to Aville about Mr. World's radio transceiver rather than visit
scenes.text_anchor: I’m not familiar with him, so I shouldn’t rashly pay him a visit.

scenes.setting: City of Silver, the Berg household then the steeple library: Derrick heeds The Hanged Man's caution, checks merit-point exchanges, and pulls out 'Giant King's Court -- Book of Blackrock, Hand-copied Edition' bound in monster hide, while Colin Iliad watches quietly from the upper level
scenes.text_anchor: “Giant King’s Court—Book of Blackrock, Hand-copied Edition.”

scenes.setting: Wednesday 12 January, 5:40 p.m., Room 312 of the White Agate in a storm off Bayam: Danitz muses on the sea while Klein reflects on how playing Gehrman Sparrow teaches him who he really is; then 'You can tell me about the pirate point of contacts in Bayam'
scenes.text_anchor: “You can tell me about the pirate point of contacts in Bayam.”

scenes.setting: 6:15 p.m., the White Agate docks at Bayam, the City of Generosity: in the corridor Klein meets Donna's family, Cleves and the others; Urdi Branch asks how to hire Mr. Sparrow (an advert for Damir's cured meat in the Sonia Morning Post), Donna asks why he chose the power -- 'For my dream... And... protect' -- then Klein tells Danitz 'You're free'
scenes.text_anchor: “Uncle Sparrow, s-since that kind of power definitely brings about threats and madness, w-why did you choose to have it?”

scenes.setting: Bayam dock: Klein walks down the gangway and heads straight for Coastal Street without looking back, while Danitz stands on the deck unable to believe a 3,000-pound bounty is being let go
scenes.text_anchor: Are you really going to let me go?

scenes.setting: Danitz doubles back through the streets to make sure he isn't followed, reaches the Golden Dream's contact house by the dock warehouses, knocks three long and three short, and gloats that he only gave Sparrow the hostile pirate contacts
scenes.text_anchor: Danitz knocked happily on the door—three long and three short—rhythmically.

scenes.setting: Old Rinn opens the door and coughs him in; Danitz smells Lanti Proof instead of Bayam Black Rand and a tall, dark, muscular man with marble-curled hair rises: 'Steel' Maveti, second mate of the Admiral of Blood, bounty 6,000 pounds
scenes.text_anchor: “Steel” Maveti! Danitz’s pupils contracted sharply.

scenes.setting: Coastal Street as the storm breaks: Danitz staggers up gutted and dying, gasps his last words to Gehrman Sparrow -- Old Rinn is compromised, Steel Maveti did it for the treasure, his title deeds on Amyris Avenue, money to his parents in Elema Town -- and Klein heals him with a swipe of Damage Transfer, having waited 'for you to finish. That's basic courtesy.' They go to find a hotel; a pirate is richer than Klein
scenes.text_anchor: “Waiting for you to finish.

scenes.setting: Empress Borough: Audrey, about to leave Backlund, concocts the Psychiatrist potion in her chemistry laboratory with Susie watching the whole process from inside the room ('Woof!'), then raises her head and downs it
scenes.text_anchor: Converging her emotions, Audrey raised her head and downed the Psychiatrist potion bottle.

scenes.setting: Audrey's chemistry laboratory, Empress Borough: the Psychiatrist potion goes down like ice cream and champagne, then golden scales crawl over her skin and her eyes turn vertical — Susie's 'Don't be afraid, calm down' pulls her into a Spectator state until the scales recede. She inventories her new powers (Awe, Frenzy, Psychological Cue, Placate, Telepathy), reshapes the Hanged Man's silver mask into an earring and christens it 'Lie'
scenes.text_anchor: “From today, your name is Lie. The most beautiful lie~”

scenes.setting: 48 Acid Lemon Street, the Wind of Azure Inn, Bayam, rain lashing the windows: Danitz splints his shattered left arm with rags while Klein asks 'What treasure?' — the unrusted black iron key from a sunken ship that the pirates call Death's Key, why Admiral of Blood Senor is after Vice Admiral Edwina Edwards, a Second-Epoch relic that 'doesn't look like the kind used by humans'. Klein orders him to write down everything Admiral of Blood and Steel Maveti have done: 'If it's appropriate, I want to hunt them.'
scenes.text_anchor: “If it’s appropriate, I want to hunt them.”

scenes.setting: Same suite, same night: an excited Danitz scribbles the Admiral of Blood's crimes in Ancient Feysac and briefs Klein on Senor (a suspected evil spirit — Wraith — with a luck-granting mystical item, seven or eight ships, flagship Tree of Flesh and Blood, 42,000-pound bounty) and on Steel Maveti, the flagship's second mate who summons zombies and rears puppets. Danitz is put in charge of gathering information on Steel; Klein, at the rain-streaked window: 'Tonight, Gehrman joins the hunt.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Tonight, Gehrman joins the hunt.”

scenes.setting: The Cathedral of Waves, Bayam, the morning after the storm: Alger, about to sail for a Wind-blessed ingredient, is summoned by the white-haired, bulging-muscled Diocese Bishop Chogo and ordered to investigate the rumor that Vice Admiral Iceberg has received Death's Key. Alger privately plans to go through the motions — 'May the Storm be with you!'
scenes.text_anchor: “Investigate this matter.”

scenes.setting: The square outside the cathedral, scattered leaves and puddles after the storm: Alger decides to tour the places where pirates roam to put on a show of working hard — and to pocket any bounty of a few hundred pounds he happens to meet
scenes.text_anchor: liquid cash flow that could be added to his savings

scenes.setting: Quarter past eleven, Bayam: Alger checks his pocket watch — only the gambling dens are open — and walks without a wrong turn to a gang-owned casino in a secluded alley where pirates fence their loot. Inside, scanning the few early gamblers, he instantly sees through someone's disguise
scenes.text_anchor: he instantly recognized the identity of a disguised person

scenes.setting: The Texas Poker table: Alger pats the disguised Danitz on the shoulder and whispers 'Blazing'. Over the cards they trade — 'I heard that your captain obtained Death's Key?', the key 'might belong to the giants or devils', Iceberg's shipboard reading lessons, Danitz's splinted arm and his wish to be told where Steel Maveti is. From 'You wouldn't know' Alger makes his bold guess and asks 'Was Bansy Harbor fun?' — Danitz's 'How did you know?' confirms Mr. Fool's adorer is his helper. Dead-drop agreed at 15 Amyris Avenue; 'Don't forget my payment.'
scenes.text_anchor: “Was Bansy Harbor fun?”

scenes.setting: Danitz alone at the table watching the captain of the ghost ship leave: 'This fellow isn't bad' — but he doesn't trust him enough to stay, in case Alger comes back with Steel Maveti's pirates
scenes.text_anchor: “This fellow isn’t bad.

scenes.setting: A department store on the street outside the casino: Alger, in local baggy pantaloons, buys a deck of tarot cards with a handful of bronze pennies and idly wonders what the adorer of Mr. The Fool is doing right now
scenes.text_anchor: “Give me a deck of tarot cards.”

scenes.setting: Old John's Restaurant, Bayam: a waiter sets down straw-wrapped, spice-crusted grilled stickleback — and two chopsticks, 'inspired by the customs of the elves' (Klein's suspect: Roselle Gustav). Klein recalls a fruitless morning of hospice visits at the church hospitals looking for a dead man to impersonate, and decides to try the adventurers' bar next
scenes.text_anchor: Chopsticks? Klein was shocked.

scenes.setting: Old John's Restaurant, finishing the stickleback: Klein muses on natives opening a Rorsted-cuisine restaurant in Backlund and on how class limits vision, pays 2 soli 5 pence (his expenses lately covered by Danitz)
scenes.text_anchor: his main expenses had been paid for by Danitz recently

scenes.setting: The street outside Old John's: a native policeman driving off a tramp snaps to a salute at the sight of Klein's frock coat and civilized cane — 'You speak good Loenese' — while the narration lays out the Mid Sonia Company's corrupt rule, the Crown's takeover of the Rorsted Archipelago, and how natives and mixed-bloods dress differently from the black-clad Loenese
scenes.text_anchor: “You speak good Loenese.”

scenes.setting: 2 p.m., the Swordfish Bar, adventurers' notice boards by the counter: Klein nurses a three-pence Zarhar for nearly an hour, listening, until four men at a nearby table mourn a lone adventurer named Wendt found dead at home with white mushrooms growing on his body and a room full of insects. Klein learns the address — 47 Blackhorn Street — and heads out
scenes.text_anchor: “A glass of Zarhar.”

scenes.setting: Wendt's rented room at 47 Blackhorn Street, found with the 'room that recently had someone die in' cane trick: Klein sets up a spirit-channeling ritual before the bed and, as a Faceless, sees the dead man's lingering spirituality (visions only: Wendt picking a green gem off a discarded corpse, Wendt dying under the mushrooms with the gem on a necklace, a flaxen-haired girl called Raine by the sea — 'I want you to marry me…'). Cause of death: an unrecognized Beyonder characteristic worn against the skin
scenes.text_anchor: “The room that recently had someone die in.”

scenes.setting: Leaving 47 Blackhorn Street after questioning Wendt's neighbors disguised as a policeman: Symeem Island, two liners a day, no relatives — only Raine, the girl he never told. Klein cringes at confessing on a dead man's behalf, sketches a plan from remembered novels and films, and boards a rental carriage hoping Miss Magician's radio transceiver comes soon
scenes.text_anchor: By the time he left 47 Blackhorn Street

scenes.setting: Backlund, Cherwood Borough: Fors skims the letter from the science-fiction novelist Aville that Xio brought back — three radio transceivers, the dearest just twelve pounds — and, spoiled by the Tarot Club's hundreds-of-pounds deals, decides to bill Mr. World postage, transport and ritual materials on top. Drizzle outside; she waits on The Sun's Spirit Eater stomach pouch
scenes.text_anchor: Fors opened a letter Xio had brought back.

scenes.setting: The Berg household, City of Silver: with the Spirit Eater's stomach pouch and Mr. Hanged Man's materials ready, Derrick decides to wait until the Chief is away on an expedition or a ritual before sacrificing them, and reads on in the hand-copied 'Giant King's Court — Book of Blackrock': a Court of God frozen in eternal dusk
scenes.text_anchor: be careful, be cautious!

scenes.setting: Waymandy's house, Hillston Borough, Backlund: by the fireplace, Emlyn fishes for the City of Silver; the 200-year-old vampire baron (black hair combed back, dark red shirt, brown pipe) knows no such city before the Cataclysm — but a Kingdom of Silver under the Giant King's Court that worshipped the queen Omebella rather than the Giant King Aurmir
scenes.text_anchor: But there was a Kingdom of Silver

scenes.setting: Wind of Azure Inn, 3:40 p.m.: Klein divines the street clear and finds Danitz already back in the reclining chair, drinking. Danitz's rounds included a ghost-ship captain named Alger who knew about Bansy Harbor — 'Very messy hair, dark blue in color?' — and Klein privately places The Hanged Man. Then the other way to find Steel Maveti without waiting: 'Use bait.' Danitz, realizing who the bait is, grabs his coat for the Red Theater
scenes.text_anchor: “Use bait.”

scenes.setting: About to tail Danitz, Klein hears layers of illusory prayer from a man and steps into the washroom instead
scenes.text_anchor: he heard layers of illusory prayers

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog: The Hanged Man's crimson star pulses with his prayer — he met Blazing Danitz at a casino, learned he witnessed Bansy Harbor and is joining a powerful figure against Steel Maveti, and suspects Danitz is working with Mr. Fool's adorer; he offers help. Klein weighs it, then conjures the fog-shrouded World dummy in a praying stance and throws its 'Honorable Mr. Fool, I am in need of some assistance' into The Hanged Man's star
scenes.text_anchor: “I suspect that Blazing Danitz is working with your adorer

scenes.setting: 5 p.m., Pam's Divination Lodge on Olive Tree Avenue, Bayam: Alger, now in a dark classical robe and clergyman's biretta, orders Fermo coffee and lays The Hanged Man face-up on a fresh tarot deck, waiting without a trace of anxiety
scenes.text_anchor: He ordered a cup of Fermo coffee

scenes.setting: Klein arrives (glasses off, face slightly altered) and sits down opposite Alger 'for a divination': The World inverted, then Hierophant / Moon / Sun as a coded plan -- tip off the Church of Storms about Blazing and Steel Maveti, beware the dream Sealed Artifact -- Klein rights the World card to accept, they fix the Amyris Avenue contact point, trade 'Let us praise God', and Klein leaves with a jab at Alger's outfit. To Alger this is Mr. World in the flesh
scenes.text_anchor: “I’d like to have a divination.”

scenes.setting: Alone again in the cafe, Alger studies himself in the corner mirror and finally sees why a boorish, hardened sea-dog should not be wearing a warlock's classical robe
scenes.text_anchor: took a good look at himself

scenes.setting: Cathedral of Waves: back in his own clothes, Alger uses a confession to reach Bishop Chogo and lays out the plan -- leak Blazing's contact point so Steel Maveti's gang walks into the Mandated Punishers; his reappearance at prayer will mean Steel is idle, his absence that the trap has sprung
scenes.text_anchor: “Very good. The way you do things is better than I expected.”

scenes.setting: 7:15 p.m., Amyris Leaf Bar by the boxing ring: Alger, in baggy pants and a head towel, plants the bait on a swarthy thin man at the counter -- 'Blazing fooled me', Steel is in Bayam, met him at the Gold Coin Casino -- and the man leaves 'in a hurry' while Alger watches his back without a smile
scenes.text_anchor: “I heard that Steel has arrived in Bayam.”

scenes.setting: Past eight o'clock: Alger leaves the Amyris Leaf Bar, walks Bayam's gas-lit streets and turns into a dead-end alley reeking of urine and alcohol, wondering whether his act needs more selling
scenes.text_anchor: Alger pulled off his headscarf

scenes.setting: Under the crimson moon a voice from behind -- 'Did you purposely leak the information about Blazing to us?' -- and Alger 'recognises' Calm Squall, Steel Maveti's chief helper (boat-shaped hat, scalpel spinning in his palm). They haggle the tip down to 300 pounds on condition Alger is detained until Blazing is caught, and Alger gives up 15 Amyris Avenue
scenes.text_anchor: “Calm Squall?”

scenes.setting: A nondescript house: Old Quinn, the Admiral of Blood's intelligence man, greets 'the blue-haired captain of a ghost ship', leads them by candle lamp into a windowless basement and locks the heavy stone door on Alger -- without disarming him
scenes.text_anchor: “Long time no see, blue-haired captain of a ghost ship.”

scenes.setting: Squall shakes any tail, rides to a garden bungalow in Bayam's Loen enclave and reports to Steel Maveti (thick lips, swarthy, steel-ball curls, a dead man's chill) among puppets and zombies; Blood Brambles Hendry twirls a straw hat on the couch as Squall proposes leaking the date to John Smith's undercover man Mordor so the adventurers spring any trap first (the other pirates lounge around them unnamed)
scenes.text_anchor: “Is the intel reliable?”

scenes.setting: Early hours: Hendry unrolls the peacock-blue Flying Carpet, Maveti, Squall, two more Beyonders and eight zombies and puppets board, 'Flight!', and the night-sky handkerchief hides them as they hover above a tree crown across from 15 Amyris Avenue through the night, watching for dawn
scenes.text_anchor: recited a single word in Elvish

scenes.setting: At first light a black-cloaked figure with yellow eyebrows and dark blue eyes crosses the rooftops and slides down the chimney of 15 Amyris Avenue -- 'none other than Blazing Danitz!' -- the pirates' spirits lift, and figures burst from Units 13, 14 and 17 to storm the house
scenes.text_anchor: It was none other than Blazing Danitz!

scenes.setting: The Church of Storms' side of the ambush: Deacon Cordoba Roye lies in wait with two Mandated Punisher teams and Sealed Artifacts 2-37 and 2-166, and runs the file on 2-37 'Dream of Eternity' through his head -- a black holed heart that traps all around it in an endless dream, its keepers confessing love to their gloves
scenes.text_anchor: “Name: Dream of Eternity.

scenes.setting: Cordoba sees 'Blazing Danitz' reach the contact point and figures dash for the house; 2-37 is lifted from its boiling water and a flute note drowns 15 Amyris Avenue in darkness. Inside, Adventurer John Smith's crew 'capture' the black-cloaked Blazing in a dream while their bodies swim on the floor; 'Move out!' -- Cordoba rushes in as 2-166 fills the living room with sunlight and holy-water rain
scenes.text_anchor: “Move out!”

scenes.setting: On the hovering carpet the pirates realise it is a Church trap -- 'he actually defected to the Church of Storms!' -- then spot 'Blazing' slipping away through the shadows. Squall leaves the two Beyonders with the zombies to make chaos, the carpet cuts ahead, Maveti freezes the shadow, Hendry's brambles bind it, and Squall's scalpel takes the head -- which shrinks into a tattered paper figurine
scenes.text_anchor: he actually defected to the Church of Storms!

scenes.setting: A hunger from the dark presses on Maveti -- 'No, it's not Blazing!' -- a compressed white-hot fireball comes off a rooftop (the real Danitz, at range), and out of the flames walks a figure in Danitz's black cloak with neatly combed black hair and cold, emotionless eyes: the 'Danitz' all along was Faceless Klein, Gehrman Sparrow
scenes.text_anchor: No, it’s not Blazing!

scenes.setting: The ten-second hunt on Amyris Avenue: lightning eyes (Interrogator's Psychic Piercing) stagger Maveti, Light of Holiness melts the Zombie like a candle, Fire Ravens and Air Bullets, a bottle of Sun Holy Water stuffed into his wound; Squall's Shriek charm drops Hendry, whom Danitz -- on a far rooftop -- finishes with a fireball; Klein shoots the fleeing Squall in the head and Creeping Hunger eats him, then wraps Maveti's corpse in the Flying Carpet, salutes the approaching Punishers and vanishes in crimson fire
scenes.text_anchor: Priest of Light, Light of Holiness!

scenes.setting: Cordoba Roye arrives with the rest of the team to scattered corpses, scalpels and withered trees, a receding aura of the sun and an evil sensation from the depths of flesh and blood
scenes.text_anchor: Cordoba Roye led the rest of the team and rushed over

scenes.setting: Dawn, a rubble-strewn alley far from Amyris Avenue: Klein, moving through shadow in Danitz's cloak, dumps Maveti's body off the carpet and Grazes him -- Creeping Hunger's skin-glove opens its red eyes, Maveti's spirit body screams soundlessly and is drawn in, yielding three powers (Zombie critical strike, ice, zombie control) but not the steel body. Klein takes only the 26 pounds, spits at the Rose School trinkets, lays the '6,000 pounds' bounty notice over the face, burns a paper figurine and phases away
scenes.text_anchor: He wanted to finish the Grazing

scenes.setting: Two or three minutes later Cordoba Roye and part of his team reach the alley just as a breeze lifts the bounty notice off Steel Maveti's dissolving, wide-eyed face
scenes.text_anchor: Cordoba Roye rushed over with a portion of the Mandated Punisher team

scenes.setting: Back at the battle site with Steel's corpse: 'A believer of the Sun?' -- Knowledge Keeper Berg, the team's Sequence 7 Reader, reads the scene as a mystical item spanning Sun and Secrets Suppliant domains, not a Sun believer or the Aurora Order; Blood Brambles was Blazing's kill, the helper 'not weaker than a Pirate Admiral'; Cordoba floats Edwina and orders the scene cleaned and a report filed
scenes.text_anchor: “A believer of the Sun?”

scenes.setting: Old Quinn's sealed basement: Alger's sight blurs and he receives The World's report to Mr. Fool -- 'the matter has come to a successful conclusion' -- (vision only: The Fool on the high chair, The World's blurry silhouette praying below). Then mint extract on the nose, a Full Moon Essence Oil mask, Emlyn's Sanguine anaesthetic gas fed through the door crack, and a Raging Blow that shatters the lock; he walks out past the sleeping guards. (Author's note on Grazing vs Devouring.)
scenes.text_anchor: Raging Blow!

scenes.setting: Early morning outside the Wind of Azure Inn on Acid Lemon Street: Danitz clings to a wall corner, replaying last night's fight and concluding that Gehrman Sparrow is the current owner of Creeping Hunger -- then, unwilling to lose his Shadow Cloak, clenches his teeth and goes in
scenes.text_anchor: Gehrman Sparrow is the current owner of Creeping Hunger!

scenes.setting: The dark luxury suite: Gehrman sits with his back to the window while Danitz reports that he tipped off the news agencies; the heads 'weren't taken', so Danitz gets five seconds to choose 3,000 pounds or the Flying Carpet -- 'Counted inwardly.'
scenes.text_anchor: “You have five seconds to consider. Exceeding that time will be considered as forfeiting.”

scenes.setting: Cathedral of Waves, morning prayers: Alger gives Bishop Chogo his edited account of the night (the Sanguine gas became a Slumber Charm) and is promised 6,000 pounds of the bounty; he plans how to launder The World's 3,000-pound share
scenes.text_anchor: “Holy Lord of Storms!” An excited Alger pounded his left chest with his fist.

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog in The Fool's high-back chair: Klein wrestles with keeping his promise to release a soul from Creeping Hunger, rejects selling the Psychiatrist (Justice is short of money) and, as a former Nighthawk, chooses the Nightmare
scenes.text_anchor: Without any hesitation, he released the Nightmare.

scenes.setting: Above the gray fog: the released Nightmare -- a black-haired, blue-eyed Red Glove from the Nighthawks -- tells how his team died hunting Death's chronicles in Qilangos's attack, names himself Davy Raymond and his daughter Neelu in Conant City, names the tycoon Jimmy Necker, and dissolves; Klein promises to visit the girl, then returns to the real world and recalls Creeping Hunger
scenes.text_anchor: “My name is Davy Raymond.

scenes.setting: The suite bedroom, too late for sleep: Klein reviews last night's lessons -- he overestimated the Mandated Punishers' patience; the Psychic Piercing + purification combo against the Lunatic-hardened Steel Maveti was the right call -- then checks his watch at nearly nine and opens the bedroom door
scenes.text_anchor: The biggest lesson for Klein was that he had overestimated the patience of the Mandated Punishers.

scenes.setting: The suite's living room: Danitz snores in the reclining chair, wakes as Gehrman takes his hat, asks if he may leave -- 'You have always been free... But that ends now.' Gehrman wants to meet his Captain: 'I have some things to ask her.'
scenes.text_anchor: “But that ends now.”

scenes.setting: Direct continuation: Danitz frowns as he watches Gehrman Sparrow walk out of the suite, unsure what he really wants with the Captain
scenes.text_anchor: Danitz frowned as he watched Gehrman Sparrow leave the room

scenes.setting: Alone in the suite, Danitz reasons his way to 'a powerful and secretive organization behind Gehrman Sparrow', fears for his Captain's 26,000-pound bounty, finds the Flying Carpet and Shadow Cloak untouched, and resolves to stay put rather than lead anyone to her
scenes.text_anchor: I will not bring danger to Captain!

scenes.setting: Quarter past three, Symeem Island: Klein steps off the five-hour liner in cheap local pantaloons and a brown cap, wearing an unremarkable native face (no named guise), tallies his fortune at 7,110 pounds, and walks into the bronze-skinned port town thinking about the Nightmare characteristic and Little Sun
scenes.text_anchor: A quarter past three in the afternoon, Symeem Island.

scenes.setting: (Klein wearing the dead sailor Wendt's face) The winery at the town's edge: wearing the dead sailor Wendt's tall thin face, Klein 'acts' the confession Wendt never made -- Raine calls him a coward and chases him off with a broom; he puts her to sleep with a charm so it will feel like a dream, watches her wake and curse 'Wendt, you selfish bastard!', feels the potion digest a little, and changes his face again
scenes.text_anchor: “Raine, I like you. I wish to marry you.

scenes.setting: Symeem Harbor's main street, native face on: Klein drops a forged police 'death notice' for Wendt into the green mailbox, weighs how cruel his staged dream was for Raine, and walks to the town's only inn thinking about the Faceless principle of disguise-and-feedback
scenes.text_anchor: This was a “death notice” he had forged as an imitation of an official police document.

scenes.setting: The inn counter: with an invented native face and no ID, Klein is refused a room; his soli note only frightens the thin boss -- 'Get out, get out, you dirty bastard with no proof of identity' -- and money loses its power for once
scenes.text_anchor: “Then you cannot stay here. This is the rule of our town.”

scenes.setting: Back as Gehrman Sparrow with a Backlund accent: the same boss now bows, forgets all about identification, and personally shows him to a clean quiet room upstairs at 1 soli 5 pence a night -- 'This really is a pragmatic world'
scenes.text_anchor: turning back into Gehrman Sparrow with stark facial features.

scenes.setting: Dinner by the ground-floor fireplace: grilled skewers, spiced mushroom soup and Gurney Sap while Klein sizes up a greenish-gray-eyed woman adventurer and her three weathered companions -- fresh mud on their boots means they came from the island's forest; then early to bed
scenes.text_anchor: Their boots have some fresh mud on them… Did they just come back from the forest?

scenes.setting: Middle of the night, 8-9 degrees: Klein braves the cold with the Sun Brooch to use the washroom, his spiritual perception fires, a venomous snake drops from the vent -- 'Bang!' -- and he pulls out a gold coin to divine
scenes.text_anchor: It was a venomous snake extending its forked tongue!
